customize.text:
One of the six heroes of Natlan named Menilek, who wielded Pyro, was born into the Flower-Feather Clan over five hundred years ago. He bore the Ancient Name
the first bearer of which was Lianca, the founder of the tribe and companion of the first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque. Menilek's Saurian companion was the Qucusaurus, Holawaqa Ngoubou, who bore a special mark on its horn. This mark is called the
Blessing, and Saurians with this mark often possess incredible abilities, but the bodies of modern Saurians cannot withstand such power. The Wayob and the Night Kingdom reject this power and refuse to accept such Saurians. As they grow older, this power either kills them or drives them mad. Legend has it that one must find a gift divided into two parts and make a pilgrimage to the Great Volcano of Tollan. There, the tribal warriors could wash away the name of their companion, which the late Xiuhcoatl remembered, and remove the mark so that the Night Kingdom could accept them.
When Ngoubou was still a small, sickly whelp, dying in Menilek's arms, the hero heard a prophecy from a sage:

<color=#ffffffd9>"Hear my last words, O hero bearing the name 'Transcendence'"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"The calamity that flows within its veins is more ancient still than your very name"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"If you yet pity mortals like your ancestors once did"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Then sever its neck and grant it the joy of freedom"</color>

But Menilek ignored these words and touched the young Saurian's bloodstained feathers with precious elixir, utterly ignoring the sigh that marked the sage's departure. The hero believed that no one and nothing could force the descendants of the Flower-Feather Clan to bend their knees. And if a curse had bound the Qucusaurus from birth, he should follow the example of his ancestors and break these chains. And so, Menilek and his loyal companion Ngoubou embarked on a pilgrimage, and legends were told of their journeys. One day, the hero tore the mountains apart with thunderous bowstrings, and the whelp used cunning to pierce the wicked python's throat. They fought a huge monster for forty days, and they finally vanquished it using a single fish. Menilek fought the warlike Tenoch even before the latter was exiled from the tribe.

But the hero and his companion were never able to complete their pilgrimage. Five hundred years ago, Natlan was engulfed by a
and Menilek admired the bravery and courage of Tenoch, who set out to unite the warring tribes and gather six heroes bearing the Ancient Names of the first Pyro Archon's companions. Menilek and Ngoubou joined Tenoch and fought shoulder to shoulder with him against the black wave. Menilek convinced himself that tomorrow, tomorrow, and tomorrow again they would complete their pilgrimage, but tomorrow never came. Along with the other heroes of Natlan, Menilek and the Pyro Archon set out for their final battle and never returned. Although the hero of the Flower-Feather Clan drank himself into oblivion before the battle, he fought bravely and, even after death, did not release the monster from his grip.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Ngoubou, my loyal companion, please rest here for a while"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"I'll be back as soon as I finish, so get a good night's rest"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Once the dark tide has subsided, I will hurry back to your side and wake you"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"And once spring returns to the earth, I shall go with you to see the new flowers blooming on the high cliffs"</color>

After Menilek’s death, Ngoubou was left alone, and under the influence of the Flamelord’s Blessing, its body acquired a supernatural form. It lost its mind, and people called it the Tyrant of the Golden Flame.

During the war with the Abyss, the Natlanese calculations estimated that they would have a maximum of five hundred years before the Night Kingdom was completely lost to the Abyss, but at that time, Natlan lay in ruins, and the civilization was dying. It was necessary to unite the tribes. Otherwise, it would be impossible to dream of a final victory. So, the Archon had a long and involved discussion with the heroes of each tribe, and finally came up with a five-hundred-year-long plan to save Natlan. During this time, the Archons and chiefs were to rebuild the tribes, and when the time came, the Wayob would again choose six heroes of Natlan with the Ancient Names of Xbalanque's companions. Haborym placed her life within the Sacred Flame in order to be reborn in five hundred years and carry out her plan. Five hundred years later, when the Pyro Archon was reborn, the Flower-Feather Clan's peacemaker, Chasca, lost her sister in a battle with the Abyss, and this pain awakened her Ancient Name, Vuka. At that moment, the spirit of Menilek appeared to her and recognized her as the new hero of Natlan. And when the time came to fight the Abyss, he helped her empower the Pyro Archon to defeat it.

<color=#ffffffd9>"My life's suffering shall be my epitaph."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"To remember the pain I endured, and finally, transcended."</color>

customize.desc: One of the six tribes of Natlan, also known as Tlalocan. The tribe's people live alongside the Qucusaurs.

customize.name: Khaenri'ahn cataclysm
customize.desc: A disaster that occurred 500 years ago. The Abyss was released into Teyvat and Khaenri'ah was destroyed.

customize.name: Goldflame Qucusaur Tyrant
customize.desc:
A Qucusaurus whose body has attained a supernatural form due to enduring forces that the bodies of modern Saurians cannot control.
Legends say that when the giant Qucusaur who now often dwells in the mountain fog was young, he also once followed the heroes who saved Natlan in their adventures. It is said that one of those heroes once agreed to make the pilgrimage with him together to the volcano, to save his mind back from the brink of insanity that the increasing violent power in his blood was forcing him towards. However, judging from his current title of "Tyrant," that story did not have a happy ending.

customize.name: Tenoch
customize.desc: A hero of Natlan, who lived 500 years ago. He didn't belong to any tribe, because he was exiled. During the Cataclysm, he united the six tribes and went to the western islands to fight a giant black monster.

customize.name: Mavuika
customize.desc: The leader of Natlan who inherited the Ancient Name of "Kiongozi." She made a vow to illuminate the future of the nation of war with the Sacred Flame.

customize.name: Xiuhcoatl
customize.desc: The Pyro Sovereign, defeated by the first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque. He faked his own death, after which the descendants of the ancient dragons could only bow before the throne and watch as their civilization inevitably faded away with each passing day.

customize.name: Chasca
customize.desc: The Peacemaker of the Tlalocan, the ender of all disputes.

customize.name: Flower-Wreathed Feathers
customize.desc: A longbow that burns like a flame. The feathers that adorn it are said to have come from the ancient tyrant Ngoubou.
